items.title: Resident Evil Reboot: Why the Film’s Past Matters
items.body: Variety’s article on Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil reboot comes with a spoiler alert, warning readers that it contains major plot revelations for the film (S6E1). The piece reminds us that the Resident Evil series is one of the longest‑running horror video‑game franchises and once held the record as the highest‑grossing film adaptation of a game, eclipsed only by Universal’s Super Mario movies (S6E1). Behind the scenes, the original games began as scary third‑person shooters, a legacy the new movie attempts to echo (S6E2). Whether these nods deepen the narrative or serve as fan service is a point fans continue to debate.

items.title: Epictetus’s Stoic Ethics: Volition and the Use of Impressions
items.body: Epictetus (c. 50‑c. 135 CE) is remembered as a Greek exponent of Stoic ethics, noted for the consistency and power of his moral thought and for effective teaching methods (S7E1). His chief concerns are integrity, self‑management, and personal freedom, which he conveys by urging students to examine two central ideas: the capacity he calls “volition” (prohairesis) and the correct use of impressions (chrěsis tō n phantasiṣn) (S7E2, S7E3). These themes underline the Stoic emphasis on inner control and rational judgment.

items.title: Messier 33: The Triangulum Galaxy in New APOD Image
items.body: NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) showcases Messier 33, the Triangulum Galaxy, a face‑on spiral system in the northern constellation Triangulum (S2E3). Also known as the Pinwheel Galaxy, M33 spans over 50,000 light‑years, making it the third‑largest member of the Local Group after Andromeda (M31) and the Milky Way (S2E4). Located roughly 3 million light‑years from our galaxy, it is thought to orbit Andromeda as a satellite (S2E5). The image highlights its loosely wound spiral arms and bright star‑forming regions, offering a striking view of galactic evolution.

discussion.body: A four-hour doc on Musk is either definitive or self-indulgent. Gibney's track record suggests the former, but that runtime demands serious commitment from distributors and audiences.
The legal threats themselves are the marketing hook. Musk trying to suppress it guarantees more attention than a quiet release ever would.
Universal's decision to proceed internationally while the US release remains uncertain suggests they're calculating where the legal risk is lowest and the audience appetite highest.
